utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case Number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please take a seat. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, Julian Nicholls, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: David Cunningham and Aleksandar Vujic, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just to flag up. It can really be dealt with at the end of the day. I'm anxious to know firstly confirmation that the witness listed for next week is actually coming, and then to know who's coming after that. I know there has been some problems, and we're told that the list of witnesses probably won't be coming, or at least one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let me --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I say, Your Honour, I've mentioned it to Mr. Cunningham, and he's going to make inquiries at the break with Mr. Ackerman, but I think the Court and ourselves --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I think my first concern first and foremost and another priority, is whether the next witness for whom we dedicated an entire week --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the other matter I want to mention. I've already mentioned that to Mr. Cunningham. It may be that he doesn't take a whole week, so if Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham are anxious to keep momentum going, they may want to have somebody else here for Friday. It's possible that the witness may not take as long as we think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you. I mean, I'm not going to interfere with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: May I address the Court, sir. The primary witness for next week, he has been verified. He is supposed to come in on Sunday for proofing and be ready to go on Monday. That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And Ms. Korner has talked to us about several matters including, Glamoc and Laktasi municipalities, I'm going to talk about that with Mr. Ackerman, try to have an answer for her in the Court today. And I'll try to resolve what's going on with witnesses. If we're not going to use the entire week, I can assure you it's our desire to go forward and not waste a day. So I'll update the Court and counsel at the first possible moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One thing I wanted to tell you is on Tuesday -- all of next week I will be busy all mornings in sentencing hearing in Dragan Nikolic, every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't realise we were afternoons next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are afternoons next week. And on Tuesday, I have to finish at 5.00 because at 5.30 I have a medical appointment that if I don't attend to now, it will be here in the Netherlands if you cancel -- have one appointment cancelled, it's another two months. This is already overdue. So I will have to leave here at 5.00 unless I manage to postpone it. But so far, I haven't succeeded because it's in a hospital. So they stick to a schedule normally. That's about it. Otherwise I am at your convenience. Important thing is to know that this witness is coming because if he doesn't turn up, then we have problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I'll verify that during the break as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we ask whether the Court schedule could be updated because according to the schedule we've got, it says afternoon on Monday, and then mornings for Tuesday to Friday. I wonder if we could have a schedule for the rest of November, whether we're mornings and afternoons.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Normally it's posted on Tribunet, but this afternoon we will send out the updated court calendar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All I know is that when we fixed the Nikolic sentencing hearing, we checked at the time, Judge Schomburg and myself, to ensure that both cases could proceed without any hitches. And it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The reason we moved to the morning, because CMSS thought Judge Agius would always like to sit in the morning. So once we identify the chance, we put it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But the Nikolic has already been fixed for all mornings, and we will take the entire week for sure because we've got several witnesses. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think all the responsibility, if I can put it that way, should be on you. I think we would all prefer to sit in the mornings rather than the afternoons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I do try to make sure that when that is possible, we sit in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But sometimes it's just not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps there will an updated schedule later today so we can see where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner. Please, Madam Chuqing. Good morning to you, sir. Welcome back. This should be your last day in this Tribunal. And I remind you once more that you are testifying under oath on the basis of the solemn declaration that you entered earlier on in the week. Madam Korner will be proceeding with her cross-examination, and then we'll see whether there is a re-examination, and then we can call it a day. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We have a blank screen at the moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you're not the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Perhaps while it's coming back on, I hope. Your Honour, what I want to get back over is, we checked the audio tape. I simply want to go back over that slightly disputed passage. So-- because there's obviously-- it was concerning to us that there might be further errors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether he spoke with Predrag Radic or whether--

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly, and I think we've solved how this happened but the answer would be if Mr. Blagojevic would be good enough to read out that one answer that he gave which begins in English "I found out about it at the end of August" and then I'd like a translation, please, by the interpreters of what he says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And could I have a page number that he's reading --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the top of page 5 English. It's that one answer. If you could read it out, please, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, I learned this at the end of August. I bumped into the then chef du cabinet of the president of the municipality, Mr. Radic. Mr. Jazic was the chef du cabinet of the president of the municipality, Mr. Radic..

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's your added explanation. Can you just literally and slowly, please, Mr. Blagojevic, read just what your answer was that was recorded, very slowly.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I read it again?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, slowly, please. The exact words that are down there.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I learned this at the end of August when I happened to meet at the entrance into the municipal building of Banja Luka the then chef du cabinet, I believe, of the president of the municipality, President Radic. That means the chef du cabinet of the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the word -- I think what caused the confusion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate that, but obviously I don't want Your Honours or the Defence to be concerned that we made an error. It's the word "I believe" or "I mean." And it starts when he used the word "I believe," which can also I think "I mean," it was translated as he meant -- he meant Radic, and that's where the problem arose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I checked with the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Blagojevic. All right. Now, Mr. Blagojevic, I want to ask you a little bit about correspondence. As secretary to the assembly of the autonomous region, would you receive official correspondence that came to the assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And would you deal with that correspondence?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If something was topical, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if it was something that was important, would you consult with Mr. Kupresanin about whether a reply should be sent or whether it should be raised in a meeting?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was it the same when you were secretary to the crisis staff of the region? Would you deal with correspondence that came in to the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It did not arrive at the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You mean there was never -- there was never a letter addressed to the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. Really, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not a difficult question, Mr. Blagojevic. Are you saying that in -- between May and the beginning of August, not one letter came in to the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It is possible, but I really can't remember. It was 12 and a half years ago. I'm not saying that it didn't arrive.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Are you telling this Court that you can remember clearly dealing with correspondence that came in to the assembly which was prior to the crisis staff, but you can't remember about the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assembly was organised in an entirely different manner. The work of the crisis staff was an improvisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It may have been an improvisation, but I'm asking you whether or not if correspondence came into the crisis staff, you dealt with it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, even if things did arrive, I would forward them immediately to the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, or when there was a meeting, I would present that at the meeting. I would take it to the meetings, and that is the only thing I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So -- all right. So you would open official mail. If it was important, you would take it to a meeting, or else you would give it to Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to deal a little bit more, please, with the powers of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you be shown now Exhibit P116, the authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is a document from the Executive Board of the SDS dated the 24th of February. And it's a decision appointing Mr. Vukic, the in-charge coordinator for the Serbian autonomous district Krajina. It sets out his duties, to coordinate and take responsibility for the activities of the municipal boards of the SDS in cooperation with the presidents of the assembly and the SAO Krajina government to ensure the implementation of decisions, conclusions, and attitudes of the assembly of the Serbian People of BH, and to take part in the work of the SAO Krajina Crisis Staff. And it says: "The decision shall enter into force on the day of its adoption." It's signed by Mr. Djukic, and it's copied to the municipal boards of the SDS of the SJ SAO Krajina, the president of the assembly of the Serbian People of BH and the SAO Krajina government. As secretary to the Krajina government or the assembly, did you see this document?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. But it is possible. I really can't remember whether I saw this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I mean, it's an official document, isn't it? Stamped?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All the rest of it. Well, the first question is: Do you accept that this effectively makes Dr. Vukic the -- it's described as coordinator, but the head of a regional SDS board?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You see, you told us in interview, Mr. Blagojevic, page - I think we've got it up on the screen - page 15, and you'll see in front of you on a screen, Mr. Blagojevic, I hope -- you have to press the button. Do you see an answer? You were being asked questions about people who attended the regional crisis staff. And you were asked about Erceg. Can you see that? I know it's not very easy to read, at line 9. And then you said you didn't know how many times, maybe a few times, Predrag Radic attended maybe once or twice, because he didn't recognise this, and so on and so forth. And then you deal with Vukic. "He was president of the party, and he was dealing with that. If there were other meetings, those were party meetings. He was saying sometimes that he was the president of the municipal board, and then the regional board, which regional board was never established. It never existed."

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand. Which regional board?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The SDS regional board. That's what you were talking about, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People disputed his appointment as the president of the regional board. They were saying that he was never elected at any of the sessions to become the president of the regional board. And people were saying that he was a self-appointed president of the regional board.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but you knew better, didn't you, because you'd seen this decision appointing him?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it says he is charged as a coordinator. He was a member of the regional board of the SDS, and it says here he is here put in the position to be in charge of coordinating the work of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you agree that there was a regional board of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably. Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Blagojevic. You were in Banja Luka. Not "probably." Was there or wasn't there to your knowledge a regional board of the SDS? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend those sessions. I don't know how it functioned. I don't know how it operated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You may not have attended the sessions. Were you aware of press conferences being given on a regular basis by Dr. Vukic as the president of the SDS regional board?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you knew that the regional board existed. So why all this going around in circles and circles? Sometimes I start thinking this man in front of me, his memory is not his strong point. But I don't think that is the problem. I think your memory is all right. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, going back to that decision, what it says in the clearest possible terms is that he is to take part in the work of what is described as the SAO Krajina Crisis Staff. So in February of 1992, Mr. Blagojevic, you were aware, were you not, that it was intended that there should be a regional crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In February, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When this document is dated.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't know then about it's existence. There were no previous arrangements, nothing pointed to the fact that this might exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, the reason I'm pointing this out to you, Mr. Blagojevic, is because the tenor of your evidence has been throughout that the regional crisis staff was an illegal body. That's what you're trying to tell this Court, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that it was not founded on any of the decisions of the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, the SDS, to all intents and purposes, was the government of the Republika Srpska, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an institution called government headed by the prime minister and other ministers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Dzeric a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Karadzic a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Krajisnik a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was Mrs. Plavsic at that time a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on, then, please. Could you now have a look at P120, which is the next meeting of the assembly after the one we looked at yesterday of the 29th of February. And could you look, please, at the last page, just so we can see it. Again, this is one of the documents, Mr. Blagojevic, you gave to Mr. MacIntosh. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And again, it's -- were these minutes drafted by you?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we can see that in effect, it's a meeting that brought into being the decision that had been made on the 29th of February to become part of the Serbian Republic in Bosnia. And we see there that the assembly is passing various decisions, putting the constitution and laws into effect, and then the election of the president of the executive council of the autonomous region. Now, the candidates were Erceg, Mr. Beslac, and Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And is this right that the previous president had been Mr. Grahovac?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who had been dismissed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin stood for election as president of the executive council although he was already vice-president of the assembly. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know why he did that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was put forward by the representatives of the Municipality of Celinac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And as it turned out, it was decided to exclude him for the very reason that he was already the first vice-president of the assembly. And then various decisions were taken. And would you agree, these were all important decisions?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The decision to form a Security Services Centre, that's the CSB. The decision to form -- I'm sorry, which affected the security. It had to do with the security of the region. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The decision to form the petrol, Krajina-petrol. That effected the economy, of course. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was just a renaming of one company. It got a new name actually. This name, Krajina-petrol. It used to be called by a different name. So when I spoke about the decision with respect to the process ongoing in the company, then the proposal made was that it should be called Krajina-petrol.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you say you spoke about it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About what?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Are you saying you spoke in the assembly, or that's what you told us before?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, before. Yesterday, I think I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And then a decision to appoint Mr. Kondic, the director general of the payment transactions and financial supervision service of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. So that was to do with the financing, wasn't it, of the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I missed, but there was a discussion of the election and appointment of a secretary. And it was pointed out -- to the CSB, and it was pointed out that that proposal would be made by Mr. Mandic. All right. Now, finally on this topic, could you look, please, at P153. This is a document dated the 16th of April 1992. And it's got a stamp, is that right, on the top showing that it was received -- of the assembly of the autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it says it was received by Mr. Vojislav Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would that be a document that you, as secretary, would have opened and given to Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We can see that this was addressed to him because it says "Vojo Kupresanin" at the top there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Forgive me. I'm not sure -- where do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But that's a statement. The document's not actually addressed to him, is it? It's addressed to the governments of the AR, Autonomous Region of Krajina, and the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to all Serbian municipalities. It's not actually personally addressed to him, is it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I can see his signature here. He was the one who actually received the document and signed for it. I can see the signature up here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Would you have seen it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In fact, if you look at the -- there's a stamp at the end of the document. Doesn't that show it was received by somebody called Mr. Batinar [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for Banja Luka, for Banja Luka. The man didn't work in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. region. So probably this was an employee of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Anyhow, it's a document relating to the Territorial Defence, or a decision of the Serbian Republic being established, and it also says: "A state of an imminent threat of war is hereby declared. There is to be general public mobilisation..." And so on. And then there's an explanation which says, under one: The established TO staffs of newly established municipalities set up district staffs in districts. This matter is hereby placed under the jurisdiction of the government of the SAOs." And so on and so forth. So in other words, an important matter relating to defence was being placed under the jurisdiction of the governments, including the Autonomous Region of the Krajina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I get back to where we started yesterday. There is no question, is there, Mr. Blagojevic, but that these regional governments were important, functioning parts of the Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In view of their authorisations at all events, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But as a matter of practical reality, these governments, these regional governments, whatever happened later, were important for the functioning of the Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably. Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, this document is dated 16th of April. Could you rephrase the question putting it in that time frame. Because 16th of April of 1992 is quite significant. I mean, what was the situation in Bosnia at the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the point I'm now making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine so. I mean, that's why I'm asking you to go straight to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was at this stage, wasn't it, that preparations were being made - and I don't want to go into who started it or who did what - but preparations were being made for what was clearly an armed conflict or going to be an armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, let's not have probably. There you are sitting as the secretary of the Krajina assembly on the 16th of April. To your knowledge, was there about to be a conflict?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know if there was about to be a conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did the war start? When did the war start? Not the Croatian one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean when it started exactly, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did it start exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, exactly. Well, I think already in the month of April some conflict started. I think in the Brod Municipality, in actual fact, towards the end of March and the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right. So when on the 16th of April of 1992 the Serbian government decides to entrust the regional SAOs with matters of defence, how do you understand that? That the central government itself was transferring to a large extent matters of defence to the regions? Is that how you would read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at the time, the war on defence was in force giving certain authorisations to the secretariats. And probably, the minister referred to that because I can see that he refers to it on the basis of Article 68 and Article 81 of the constitution of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, really, I would like to move along. So if you could just try and concentrate on the question and answer. On the 6th of April, you do remember that the independence of Bosnia had been recognised apparently by the European Community?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it was absolutely clear to you, wasn't it, Mr. Blagojevic, that no way was the Serbian government, so-called, going to accept this?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And so for the first time, the Serbian government was using these regional authorities which had been established by them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And they were saying here a state -- or Mr. Subotic, the defence minister for the Serbian government was saying a state of threat of imminent war is hereby declared. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that was the reason for the formal declaration, wasn't it, of crisis staffs?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here they -- actually, he just refers to the secretariats which had their support in the constitution and the law on national defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, in general terms, and we're going to move on to Mr. Dzeric's instructions in a moment that you looked at. But in general terms, the reason for crisis staffs under the old Bosnian law was if the assembly was unable to meet owing to an emergency or an actual war or a threat of war. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, pursuant to the constitution, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That is why the crisis staffs in the municipality came into existence, and that is why the regional assembly formed a crisis staff. Isn't that right, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just say with respect to your latter question, if the assembly cannot meet, then what were these organs supposed to be called? I just can't remember. I don't think they were called crisis staffs. I think this organ had a different name for a state of imminent war or threat of war. I think it was called differently, if they were unable to meet and convene a session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to suggest to you they were actually called war presidencies or something like that, but the effect was the same, isn't it? It was a body derived from the assemblies together with the leaders of the police and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it should have been, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, can we look, please, again at the document that you looked at with Mr. Cunningham which is P157. Mr. Dzeric's document; excerpts, rather. And what you had to say about this when you were shown it, and this is the LiveNote for the 29th. The question was put to you by Mr. Cunningham, and it's page 54 of that LiveNote: "Does this document ever mention to the best of your knowledge regional crisis staffs?" And you said: "As far as I can see in this document, no." Question: "When you were working for the ARK, when you found out about this document, when you read it, what effect, if any, did it have on you?" "None whatsoever." Can we take it from that that you saw this document when it was issued on the 26th of April, or shortly after?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that. After that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. And how did you see it? Who gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it when it was published in the Official Gazette of the Serbian Republic because it was published in the Official Gazette fairly speedily.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And that's the direction to the municipalities as to how they should work. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But one of the things it had to do, if you look at item number 14: "The Crisis Staff shall convene and make decisions in the presence of all its members, take official minutes, issue written decisions, and submit weekly reports to the regional and State organisations..." Now, what was the regional organisation in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regional institutions, you mean, at the time. Well, all the institutions were established at the 4th of March assembly in 1992, those. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was the regional institution to which weekly reports would have to be submitted, the regional institution which was part of the government structure?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here that the crisis staffs of the municipal bodies should send to the regional bodies their reports, or rather their minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you one last time, Mr. Blagojevic: What was the regional organisation that formed part of the government of the Serbian Republic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council, the executive council of the region.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Of -- the executive council of what body?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably the regional secretariat for national defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is not talking about national defence --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- Is it? It is talking about all the duties that the crisis staff has to carry out.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This set of instructions, you mean? Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, are you deliberately trying to avoid giving the answer that you know to be the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the form of the question as being argumentative, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rephrase the question, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: With respect, I don't think that is a proper objection. I'm asking him whether he is intentionally trying to avoid it. It's not a comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, restrict it to that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you intentionally trying to avoid saying that it was the assembly of the autonomous region or whatever body represented it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I really don't know whom they sent this off to. I know that the assembly of the region, but I don't remember that a single crisis staff ever submitted a report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That was the reason, wasn't it, why the presidents of the crisis staffs of the municipality were attending the meetings of the regional crisis staff, to give a report on what was happening on their area?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yesterday what that grew into. First of all, what happened was that the composition of the body was highly diverse. And we saw the composition and the members that made it up pursuant to the decision, and then the deputies, presidents of municipal boards, municipalities came in, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The question I asked, Mr. Blagojevic, was: Isn't that why the presidents of the municipalities were attending on a weekly basis when possible meetings of the Crisis Staff of the region?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they would come and present the problems of their municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this question: Is it not because of this instruction from Mr. Dzeric that the municipalities were coming to submit -- well, actually, I'll take that back. I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can stop here, and the Trial Chamber will draw its own conclusions, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in any event, Your Honour, I don't think the question I was about to ask is one he can properly answer. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to deal with a different topic, and that is the topic of the arrival of the SOS in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if he remembers about them, first.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you remember the arrival of the SOS in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Probably he's not. Do you remember the SOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why not, Mr. President? I said that one morning when I was on my way to work, at a certain point a group of people stood in front of me and didn't allow me to pass by and sent me back. And I didn't know who these people were or what they represented. So I wasn't allowed to go to work. They sent me back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's all I know about them. At the time, that's all I knew about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you remember barricades being set up by these men?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And on my way to work, I came upon one of these barricades. That was precisely it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you were on your way to work to the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And these people had surrounded the municipal building, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And they were armed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some of them did have arms. Others didn't. The composition was different. But you could put it that way. They did have weapons, yes. I saw some people wearing camouflage uniforms without weapons whereas others did have weapons. So Mr. President, may we go into private session, please, for this part.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it's a matter for Your Honours. I'm not sure what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go for a while into private session first. And you tell me why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The moment you want to go to private session, you just ask me. And we will accede to your request if it's the case. I see you perplexed. Maybe it's a question of interpretation. I say any time -- we are back in open session now. And any time you want us to go back to private session, let me know. All right? Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I want to now talk -- ask you some questions about the crisis staff. Could you have back, please, Exhibit P168. You were asked about that yesterday, and it was put to you that all these people came from Banja Luka. I want to explore that a little further, please. Brdjanin, the president of the crisis staff, was the representative from Celinac to the Assembly of the Serbian People. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The vice-president of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was from Srbac. He lived in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Because I don't want to keep you here too long. I'm not interested in where they lived. I'm trying to establish what the positions of these people were. Do you understand? All right. Mr. Brdjanin was also the -- for some period of time the president of the executive council in Celinac.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He was a member of the Crisis Staff of Celinac?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably, by virtue of office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Sajic, he was the person in charge of the National Defence Council, is that right, in the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the secretary for National Defence, I believe, for the Banja Luka Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Kupresanin, I'll come back to him. He was also a deputy to the Assembly of the Serbian People, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he was, as we know, president of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Erceg was the president of the executive council to the assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the executive council, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic was the president of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dr. Vukic, as we've seen, was the head of the regional board or the coordinator of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dr. Milanovic, who was he? I think you did tell us in interview, but I now can't remember.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a national deputy, and he became vice-president of the National Assembly of Republika Srpska later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: General Momir Talic was the head of the 5th Krajina Corps based in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that it was the biggest corps in the whole of originally the JNA and then later the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Major Jokic, was he the air force?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what his role, or rather function was. What position he occupied. I don't know what his profession was either.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stojan Zupljanin, chief of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was chief of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And clearly, that was a vital position in Banja Luka, wasn't it, the head of the regional police force?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dr. Kuzmanovic who was later replaced. He was the director of the university?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Puvacic was the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Jovo Rosic was the judge in charge of the Banja Luka court?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then we come to Dubocanin and Stevandic. Who was Mr. Dubocanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the functions we mentioned earlier on, I'm really not clear of their position here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Blagojevic, it's right, isn't it, that the regional crisis staff was supposed of the most powerful men in the region in each of their respective spheres?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that question because how can he differentiate between the 17 members in saying whether A is the top. I just think it calls for him to make a conclusion across the board as to whether they're at the top of the region in their respective sphere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't agree with you, Mr. Cunningham. I mean, the question is a very clear-cut and important one, too, whether this regional crisis staff actually was composed as to the first 15 members of the most important people in the region. So the witness should look at those 15 names. And if he disagrees, for example, if he thinks that Dr. Kuzmanovic was not a powerful personality or person in the region, even though he was replaced, he can say so. But then I would expect him to answer with regard to the rest. So proceed. I think, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll split this. I'll split this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: General Talic was the head of the army for the whole region?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zupljanin was head of the police for the whole region?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The two leading politicians in the assembly were members of this crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This crisis staff, therefore, had real authority, didn't it, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, by virtue of the office these people held, that would be the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, I want to go back over this question of why Brdjanin and not Kupresanin became the head of this crisis staff. You've told us that -- you told us on Wednesday -- on the 29th that it was a matter of discussion at one of the sessions of the crisis staff when the deputies asked why Mr. Kupresanin as president of the assembly was not the ex officio president of the crisis staff. At what session of the crisis staff did this come up?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one of the meetings when the presidents of the municipalities and boards and the deputies came to attend. So they raised that question, the reason why Mr. Brdjanin was the presiding person and not Mr. Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you then said that Mr. Kupresanin gave an explanation to this effect, and you remember this clearly apparently, and this is at page 65 of the LiveNote: "Why should I assume responsibility, he said, for one body if the government left it to municipalities to appoint and replace directors of enterprises and all the other positions." Now, did he say that to you in private or to the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he said it at the crisis staff meeting as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can you explain to us what you meant. Can you explain what he meant by that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me -- he told me that in view of the fact of what happened on the 29th of February, that is to say, the rift between the region and the central headquarters, that this would give rise to even greater problems, make them even more profound between the region and the government on one side as it would between the municipalities and the region on the other. So at the assembly of the autonomous region held on the 29th of February, as I say, the delegates, or rather most of the delegates, the presidents of the municipalities, gave absolute support to the central powers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Precisely, except that we've just looked at a whole series of documents which show, and which I thought you'd agree with, Mr. Blagojevic, that the regional government was an essential part of the operating of the whole of the Serbian government.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but there was a decision that was made, and he referred to the decision about the organisation of companies. And pursuant to that decision, the government nominated all the directors. And generally, all the appointments at a political level, and nominations, and the Executive Boards of the municipalities would appoint directors at a municipal level. And one article of that decision stipulated that the appointed individuals would be responsible to the organs appointing them. So he kept underlining this fact and said "why should I be there when I have no authorisations?" And also, one of the reasons that he quoted was his health. He said his health was not good, and that he was getting ready to undergo heart surgery, and I think that's what happened soon afterwards. He was operated on, and I think he said that he no longer wanted to be involved in the conflict between the representatives of the municipality and himself because he was having a great deal of problems, as I said, for his clearly-worded speeches and statements at the assembly meetings. He was very sharp and came into conflict with both the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we take this, please, in stages. The appointment, or more pertinently, the dismissal of persons from companies and the like was only one part, was it not, of the function of the assemblies and then the crisis staffs?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the decision to form the war presidencies later on and the organs in the municipalities, they were given full competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. That's not the question. The question was: Appointment or dismissal of people from companies was only one part of the functions of assemblies and crisis staff, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among other things, yes. That, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, was this the situation, that Mr. Brdjanin was a much stronger personality than Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, no. Mr. Kupresanin enjoyed far more respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's a different matter. I'm talking about the personality of the two men. Was Mr. Brdjanin a more forceful personality than Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't say myself. It's difficult to assess that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've looked at some of the assembly minutes, and it's clear that -- would you agree -- I'm sorry. Would you agree that Mr. Brdjanin spoke apparently more often than Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which assembly meeting?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the assembly of the autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kupresanin was the presiding officer. And when he was presiding over the meeting, he would conduct the meeting, in fact. So there would be very little reason for him to actually take the floor. It would be the delegates who would take the floor. That's the way the assembly operated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I see. So it's because Mr. Kupresanin was in charge that he didn't speak very often?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you don't agree that Mr. Brdjanin had the more forceful personality?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that a true picture and appraisal was given by the assembly meeting that we discussed yesterday, the one that was held -- or rather, I think we mentioned it this morning where the executive council of the region was elected, where Mr. Brdjanin was put forward for president. And I don't think he received more than seven votes for being a candidate at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ask Mr. Kupresanin at any stage why he didn't -- why he wasn't on the crisis staff that was formed as a result of the SOS's demands?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that nobody called him to do that, or informed him about anything. And yet, he was president of the assembly of the region.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can we move to the question of the recording of these crisis staff meetings. You looked at the instructions that were handed out by Mr. Dzeric a moment ago. And one of these -- those instructions was to this effect, that official minutes of crisis staff meetings had to be taken. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this related to the crisis staff of the municipalities, and they did keep minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whether or not it related to the crisis staff of the municipalities, a crisis staff of the region was formed. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You had taken minutes of the meetings of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The crisis staff was replacing the assembly of the region. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way. In view of the later presence of the deputies, the presidents of the municipalities, of the executive boards and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We could put it any way we like, Mr. Blagojevic. How do you put it? It replaced the assembly, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you've told us that in your opinion, as a result of the decisions taken by the government, the assembly of the autonomous region was a lawful assembly. That's right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assembly of the autonomous region, you mean. Yes, that's right. It was based on the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it was absolutely clear to you, I suggest, from the documents which we've looked at and which you saw that the crisis staff of the region was equally, as far as the Serbian Republic was concerned, a lawful organisation?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nevertheless he had to derive his authorisations from government decisions. And all the affairs that the government was engaged in, it had to convey these competencies and authorities to the crisis staff of the region which is something it did not do. So that none of the members of the government ever asked reports from the crisis staff, nor did they attend crisis staff meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we leave that aside for the moment. I want to concentrate on the minutes, please. Can you explain to this Court why you did not take any minutes as you say you did not?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was impossible, Madam Chairman, to keep the minutes. Because the meetings were held every day, one day after another, for three days continuously, for example. And now in the municipality of the region, the assembly of the region, there was just one employee, myself. I had one office, 3 metres by 2 metres. And the investigators saw the size of that office when they were there. I had no administrative apparatus. Whereas the Banja Luka Municipality had a staff of 600 working in the administration, and the entire assembly of the region just had me, one employee. And when a meeting of that type was held, you would have 30 to 35 participants taking place, you would have to organise everything which means that I would need the technical equipment for recording the meeting, I would need a shorthand typist, and I would need other technicians and the necessary facilities. That's one point. And secondly, the meetings would go on for four or five hours, that means that we would need to type it out, prepare all the documents, and I didn't have the service to back me up to do that. So it was decided that as people took the floor, and there were no clear-cut rules on procedure for the work, as you usually have in assembly work, that presentations by members taking part in the discussion would be limited to 5, 10, or 15 minutes, there were no rules governing the work of these meetings. So I think somebody from the Serbian Municipality of Drvar, for example, a very rich area, rich in forests, he would make a 40-minute speech about the war profiteering and how the forest was being cut down. And then he would end by saying that the municipality lacked sugar, oil derivatives, flour, and things of that kind. There was a shortage of medicines and nothing was actually functioning. So there were no strict, clear-cut rules. So the agreement was reached that when somebody would take the floor, their time wouldn't be limited. And at the end of his discussion, he would propose conclusions. What he wanted to do and what he thought should be done. And he would set this out in writing, and that is what I would note down. I would note down the person's conclusions. We would then hand that on to Mr. Brdjanin. And at the end, Mr. Brdjanin would read through these proposals. So that's what it was like. Because it was absolutely impossible, not feasible, to have a meeting lasting four, five or more hours and a session going on the next day, to prepare all the minutes. You can't have good quality minutes without stenographic notes. And people would complain if you did so and say that's not what they said. So those were my problems. And as I had a lot of experience in the field, we had to improvise to a great extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So those -- and the investigators were able to make their own minds up as to that because my office was the smallest office in the Banja Luka Municipality building. It was a room 3 by 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was the problem about setting up a recording device?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't have one. Quite simply, we didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the whole of the Banja Luka Municipality, you had no recording device?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't -- we were just borrowing their premises, if I can put it that way. They gave us two rooms to use. The president of the executive board, for example, had absolute power over all the resources. He wasn't a member of that particular body. He ignored the body and never attended any meetings. Although he was president of the board, he never attended any meetings of that particular body. So, of course, we weren't lent support.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Who did you say never attended meetings of the body?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kasagic. Mr. Kasagic. Their administrative department would receive salaries, they had the necessary resources which were lacking in this other places. So we didn't have the necessary facilities. I had trouble coming by the paper we needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who told you that you need not take minutes?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite simply, it was impossible to take minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But it was your job to take minutes. Who told you need not take minutes?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all agreed that when somebody asked to take the floor, that person would make a note of his conclusions and proposals because we didn't have the necessary facilities to do things in the proper way and record things in the proper way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you say -- pause, Mr. Blagojevic. Mr. Blagojevic, you say "they all agreed..." Who agreed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But did you at some point, Mr. Blagojevic, as you must have, say to Mr. Brdjanin, as president of the crisis staff, "Look, it is impossible for me to take minutes"?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not to him. I told everyone, all those present.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But it was your responsibility to the president of the crisis staff to take minutes, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He agreed with that method of work, the one we applied, because he was fully conscious of the fact that we didn't have the necessary facilities and conditions to work as we had been doing when the other organs had the complete administrative in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The discussions and the decisions being taken were important ones, weren't they, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, they were. They were important. If you look at it that way. However, now the final implementation of those decisions is what we should take a look at.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's exactly what we are going to take a look at, Mr. Blagojevic. Didn't you think or anybody think that it would be important to keep a record of these decisions being taken in a time of conflict?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, of course. That was absolutely necessary, yes. But quite simply, what I'm saying is this: There were no technical possibilities of doing that. And as I said, the meetings were held one after another for three days. And the discussions went on for four, five, six or more hours in a single day. So this would take a stenographer two or three days to get all that down in record form. And if he were to draw up the minutes, you would have to do so over a period of several days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And this is how you described in your interview the method you say happened, that the decisions when they were made - this is at page 21 for Mr. Cunningham - someone had to type them up, someone had to approve them, someone signed them, and they were published. I'm sorry, that was the question. "Explain the process of how it went from the decision being made at a meeting to being in the Official Gazette and published in Banja Luka." And you said: "Well, they would dictate this to me. I would write it down. Then I would type it. If I couldn't type it, then I would ask a woman who worked in a typist office to help me, and then I would prepare it for publishing." Is that what you say happened still?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was a decision, a decision which was taken on the 6th. Pursuant to this decision, the secretary of the Autonomous Region of Krajina was authorised to prepare the Official Gazette for the publication of the decisions of the assembly, the crisis staff, and the executive council. I remembered only yesterday afternoon that item 2 gave the authorisation to the person under item 1 to be allowed in case of the absence of the members of the crisis staff to sign this decision. And then I also remembered that when I was looking at the signatures yesterday, I remember that I also had an authorisation pursuant to that, and I also remember that what I saw yesterday was not a forgery, that where it said "Boro Blagojevic," that indeed was my signature. For a moment, I was afraid it was a forged signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to come on to the question of signatures a little later. I want to, please, just stick to the notes.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You went on to say this, that you drafted resumes - I'm now looking at page 22 of the interview, Mr. Cunningham - and you were asked: "Did you circulate them to the members who had taken part in the discussions?" That's your resume of what had been said. And you said: "No." And you were asked: Who were the persons who saw these resumes?" And you said Brdjanin. And you said: "Brdjanin would read them to see if he would agree with them."

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when a member put forward a conclusion, he was then asked to put it in writing. This would then be submitted to Mr. Brdjanin for his perusal. And then when Mr. Brdjanin read it and when this person formulated this conclusion, I was also given the task to read it. In some of the decisions, I saw quite a number of technical mistakes being made.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you also told us, and is this right, that Mr. Brdjanin would make his own notes?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that he made his own notes in order to be able to draft his own conclusions. Because very often, it was him who proposed conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And there's no doubt about it. As you told us in interview, Mr. Brdjanin was in control, in command of those meetings. Page 19. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you one last time, Mr. Blagojevic. Are you really telling us that no minutes were recorded or kept by you of these important meetings?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. It has been asked and answered. It has been discussed in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know, I'm giving him one last opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you really telling us that, Mr. Blagojevic, that the crisis staff of the region was the only authority I suggest in the whole of Bosnia that did not keep minutes of official meetings?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure of that. It was impossible for the various reasons that I've mentioned. There was no technical possibility to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And you didn't think it was advisable to keep your own notes or resumes for the future?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just simply didn't have the conditions in place. I did not have anybody to whom I could delegate tasks. I had to perform all the duties. I had to be a stenographer and everything else. So if you look at the decisions in the Official Gazette, you will see a lot of technical mistakes that were supposed to be corrected later on. But we didn't because we just didn't have anybody to take care of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move to the Official Gazettes. All decisions passed by authorities, municipal or regional, had to be published in the Gazette. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Only the decisions passed by the regional crisis staff and the regional executive council, or if a decision was taken by the assembly of the region. Those were published.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And the reason for publication in the Gazettes is what?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason would be the consequence of the session on the 29th of February 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Don't bother about that. Can you tell me just generally --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- why are regulations, decisions, and authorities published in the Gazette -- a gazette?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was the following: People said that this would prove to the central government that we were not doing anything behind their back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is important.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm asking generally why do the decisions made by the Serbian Republic or by municipalities, why are they published in a gazette? I'm asking for the general reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As a lawyer, you should know as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a well-known fact, to make the general public aware of the decisions that were taken and how they are to be applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Now, can you have a look, please, again at Exhibit P227. You were the person, I think, Mr. Blagojevic, who gave these Gazettes to the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you remember that in April, or possibly in August 1996?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What happened to issue 1? This is the issue 2, the Official Gazette of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. What happened to issue 1?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lots of people have asked me that same question. I was going to publish the statute of the region and all the other general enactments and the decisions taken at the last session when the executive council and the secretariat, secretariats were established. That was what I was going to publish in issue number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, but do you mean it wasn't published?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not published.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I don't think I'll go down that road. Anyhow, it's right that you're shown, Mr. Blagojevic, as the editor of the Gazettes, if we look at the last page?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The assembly authorised me to prepare and to edit the Official Gazette which would carry the decisions taken by the assembly, by the executive council, and the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. So it was your job to ensure that when they went into the Gazette, they were accurate?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This should have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can I just ask you, if we can just look, please, at - and we'll need to have, I'm afraid, on the ELMO the actual B/C/S version - the first decision dated the 4th of May. After the words -- after the typed signature of Lieutenant-Colonel Sajic, do some letters appear? It's a terribly bad --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the secretariat, the secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence, the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Usher, can you take that, and I want that last line. It doesn't appear on that copy very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Do we see there the secretary of the Council for National Defence, and then the name Lieutenant-Colonel Sajic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What do the letters after his name stand for? Do you see those two letters?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SR. That is, in his own hand, his own handwriting. But let me tell you about this. This merits some attention. There were quite a number of technical mistakes. For example, it says: "The responsible people are presidents of the crisis staff of the municipalities." This is a mistake. Above that, in the original document, it says that the responsible persons are presidents of Council for National Defence. And in the original document, you can see that. And I was the one who was supposed to correct this mistake, but I didn't do it, if you look at the original document by Mr. Sajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Believe me, Mr. Blagojevic, I'm not interested in the moment in technical mistakes in the rest of document. That means -- those initials means that you confirmed that was signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Sajic in his own hand?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, now, you see, let's look at one of, or some of the signatures of Mr. Brdjanin, or some of the decisions signed by Mr. Brdjanin. If we go, please, to the 6th of May decision, which was number 3, does that show Radoslav Brdjanin as the signatory with the same letters, SR, confirming that he signed it in his own hand?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Or obviously somebody on his behalf who had put "za" on the original document?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And all the decisions that apparently were signed by Mr. Brdjanin, when they go into the Gazette --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to object, Your Honour, because based on the testimony yesterday I believe there's two, maybe three documents that he identified as being signed by Mr. Brdjanin. And I don't know of anywhere in the record where there has been any proof that he signed the other documents. Of course, I wasn't here for that part of the trial, and I will certainly trust your memory over my recollection of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham, the position is this: I think you ought to distinguish between what the witness recognised as certainly being Mr. Brdjanin's signature and the rest. But he did not exclude any of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think the point is being missed slightly by Mr. Cunningham. That's not the exercise I'm undertaking now. I know what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I understand the exercise you're taking with these two notations, the two letters after the signature. I understand that completely. I just wanted to lodge an objection -- and I think the Court recognises what I'm trying to do, and I understand Court's position as well. I just didn't want -- and I apologise for interrupting. I did not want it to be taken as some sort of concession that we're agreeing that he signed these other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From that point of view, yes, point taken and conceded. But it doesn't mean to not amount to an obstacle to Ms. Korner, for Ms. Korner to proceed with her questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, let's go ahead, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
