utterances.text: Each and every one of the documents that bear Mr. Brdjanin's signature that we have copies of are in these Gazette with those letters after that, aren't they, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would you have put those into the Gazette if you hadn't been satisfied that Mr. Brdjanin had signed those decisions?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some decisions which were not signed by him. Still, they were published. If I was about to publish my issue of the Gazette and if the minutes were not ready yet, I would still put those decisions in the Gazette even if they were not typed because there was no time between the session and the dates of the publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think -- you either did not understand the question or you avoided, tried to do your best to avoid answering it. That's not the answer that's expected of you. I'll read the question that Ms. Korner put to you again. First it was put to you that throughout this Gazette, each and every one of the documents that bear Mr. Brdjanin's signature, they also show -- carry also the two letters. And you are being asked: Would you have put those into the Gazette - that is, the CP, the confirmation that this is signed by Mr. Brdjanin with his own hands - would you have put in that declaration if you were not satisfied that those documents had indeed been signed by Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was something that was passed at a session of the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was passed at a session of the crisis staff? Were you authorised to make a false declaration, for example, say, signed by Mr. Brdjanin with his own hand when it wasn't? Would you have made that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So am I to conclude that when you put down Radoslav Brdjanin, S.R., that was because you were satisfied that indeed Mr. Brdjanin had affixed his signature to that document with his own hands? If it had been signed by someone else for Mr. Brdjanin, for example, what would you put down here? Would you put down "Radoslav Brdjanin, S.R."?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because he was president of the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if he didn't sign it himself and someone else signed it, would you declare to the public that it had been signed by Radoslav Brdjanin when it wasn't?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because whatever was adopted at sessions, we would publish it regardless of the fact whether it was signed or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us a moment ago, Mr. Blagojevic, that sometimes you published these minutes before they were signed. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand. Publish what?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That you put the minutes or the -- I'm sorry, the decisions, I should say, or the conclusions into the Gazette before they had been signed? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But supposing you'd got it wrong and that wasn't the decision that had been arrived at? Wasn't it a bit dangerous to do that? And you didn't have any minutes or notes that you could look at.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any minutes or notes. But what was concluded, we would go. We would type it. But sometimes because of a lot of duties that I had --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Go on.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- They didn't have the time to wait, to sign. In the meantime, we had to prepare the Gazette for publication, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, let's take --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was enough for us to hear something being adopted at a session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But if you had got it wrong, without minutes or recordings, you had no way of showing that this unsigned decision had been accurately recorded by you. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the following day, we would submit those to all the members, to their desks. And nobody objected to anything that was done by us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Blagojevic. These Gazettes came out long after the decisions that had been taken. This one, issue 2, was published on the 5th of June, and the last decision recorded in it was that of the -- well, actually, it's not quite right. I take that back, because it was the 3rd of June. I'm sorry, ignore that for the moment. Mr. Blagojevic, what I want to understand is this: When you put those letters, SR, after each of the decisions supposedly signed by Mr. Brdjanin, you're telling this Court that sometimes they had not been signed by Mr. Brdjanin, and sometimes they had never been signed at all. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But it was important, was it, for the people who were going to read the Gazettes to know that Mr. Brdjanin's signature, whether it was or wasn't on it in real life, was on those decisions, and that's why you put the initials SR? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. But again, this conversation shows you that this was just an improvisation, that there were no conditions in place to do it properly. For example, today there will be a session. There will be another session on the following day. We would prepare everything. On the following day, we would put the papers on their desks. There would be no objections. And things were just done in that improvised way. It was nothing but an improvisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's just deal with the signatures, please. The one and only signature of Mr. -- well, let's deal with your own, first of all. Can you have a look, please, at P273 again. That's a conclusion of the 2nd of July dealing with a, as it were, coordinating body, which included Mr. Brdjanin and others. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My signature would be only where it says "Boro." Because Brdjanin could also be signed by other members of the crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. On the document, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not your signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for a fact. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, please. Do you recognise your own signature? Did you hear the question, Mr. Blagojevic? Would you look, please, at that signature and tell us whether or not you signed that.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But it's possible. I'm not sure, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, earlier on today during the first session, he referred to a document which supposedly, as I understood, and I may be the stupid one here, but I remember him saying, referring to a document which supposedly bore his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought it was this one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. Because I heard you now say this is the only document you have which bears his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: From the crisis staff, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Earlier on today, you said -- you referred to a document which you saw yesterday, I suppose, which had your signature on it. And yesterday, you weren't quite sure. In fact, for a moment, you even said -- you even thought it was a forgery. And then you thought, and it came to your mind that that was no forgery and that was indeed your signature. Were you referring to this document? Were you shown any other document yesterday which had your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where it says "Boro," I'm sure there. I'm sure about that where it says "Boro" because I remember the decision that was made authorising me to be -- me to sign in the absence of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But which document? Which document were you referring to? Is it this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the one you mentioned earlier on today, you told us earlier on today, perhaps someone can refer me to the LiveNote page and line, that there was a document which had your signature on it, and that yesterday you weren't quite sure that it was your signature. In fact, you were even suspecting that it was a forgery. But then you had afterwards and that you came to the conclusion that that was indeed your signature. Which document were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were several documents where it clearly said "Boro." Those ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you see them yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And was that during the examination-in-chief by Mr. Cunningham or when you were being questioned by Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was Mr. Cunningham because I always have a -- I'm always suspicious when it comes to copies. Had it been an original document I could say straight away because the regular practice is for copies to be certified as corresponding to the original, they must be certified saying they are a true reflection of the original, and that must be done by the organ charged to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just a bit concerned about the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm just trying to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you saying that one of the documents that Mr. Cunningham showed you yesterday which were all concerned with whether or not Brdjanin's signature was on them, you actually saw your signature. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Where it clearly says "Boro".

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You mean you signed on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What you said signed for, that was it. Pursuant to point 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: During the next break, you can have all those documents back that Mr. Cunningham showed you, and you can tell us which ones you signed. But I want to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Can you have it in original?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They got the original, well, that photocopy originals. I don't think we have got originals of any of these, that I recall. We'll do a check, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps he can tell us whether this signature resembles your signature, at least.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it does. That first letter does resemble mine. As to the rest, I can't be sure. As I say, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I'm saying is that I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look at the only document you positively identified Mr. Brdjanin's signature on. And that is in my version P -- there is a number of different versions. P688. I can't remember the exhibit number that he was given yesterday, but it's the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I think it's 254.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 254. It's more probably 255. It's more probable 255.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, both of those, Your Honour -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: As usual, Your Honour, your recollection is right on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, can you have 688 and 255. That is the document on which you positively identified Mr. Brdjanin's signature. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do we have on the ELMO, just for the record?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's 688.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is 688.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that right, Mr. Blagojevic? You positively identify his signature?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On which document?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The one you can see on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And 255, which we'll give you back again, is a copy of that decision which was sent for immediate delivery to the president of the municipal crisis staff. If you look at the top of it, bring it down so that Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also Brdjanin's signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's headed there "for immediate delivery - in handwriting - to the president of the municipal crisis staff." Yes?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whose handwriting is that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the handwriting of Mr. Kupresanin's secretary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. So this was an important decision that had to be sent to the crisis staff presidents, the municipal crisis staff presidents. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And no doubt, you remember this decision clearly because it was the one that said non-Serbs could not hold effectively any jobs. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And so important, was it, that it was actually published in the newspaper, if you look, please, at Exhibit 254. Do you remember seeing a copy of this decision being published in Glas?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to have the Gazettes for the relevant period. Could you have, please, Exhibit P295. There's the Official Gazette published by you as editor. And it lists the decisions taken from the 9th of June onwards. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we look, please, just very quickly, we see the 9th of June, and then the next decision, the 23rd of June. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And from there, the next decision published is the 29th of June, to do with motor vehicles and the like. Right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why didn't this decision, this vitally important decision, appear in the Gazette?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite simply I decided, in agreement with Mr. Kupresanin, that that decision for us didn't merit being published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Didn't merit?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely because of the text of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you mean because it was a completely, utterly, illegal decision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, too, absolutely. That its contents really didn't merit being published, and that was highlighted by a meeting held after that where none of the presidents who were there, who attended, had any report to table in that regard pertaining to it. And so after that, I and Mr. Kupresanin, because of the contents of the decision, thought that its place, proper place, was not publication in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yet, Mr. Kupresanin's secretary sent it to the presidents of the municipality. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she did send it to the presidents of municipality to act upon it. And later on, at a crisis staff meeting, nobody tabled any reports pertaining to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's simply -- Mr. Blagojevic, that's not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You thought it was illegal; Mr. Kupresanin thought it was illegal. You didn't put it into the Gazettes because of that. Did anybody take that up with Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite simply what it said there was the responsible person was the secretary, responsible for placing the documents there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As a result of that decision, countless non-Serbs that hadn't already been dismissed were dismissed, weren't they, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I really can't remember. Because it was in 1992, you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, did you have non-Serb friends in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, of course. A very large number, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How many of them kept their jobs?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my friends, the ones I knew, kept their jobs. Practically -- or rather, a large number of them did because every morning, Mr. Emir Busatlic, a well-known Banja Luka physician, or rather a dentist, came to me every morning. And there was this other gentleman, the vice-president of the Banja Luka municipality, Mr. Tonko Ruzic, they came in every morning and they remained in their posts until the end of their term of office, both of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you remember Mr. Brdjanin giving an interview in Glas and naming people, non-Serbs, who had to be sacked?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, but quite possibly that did happen, although I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Osmancevic, Dzevad Osmancevic, the head of Metal?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. Dzevad Osmancevic was a well-known director of Metal from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was he dismissed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I was going to do this later, but --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether he was then or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us that nobody carried out that instruction in the municipalities, to your knowledge. Can you have a look, please, at P1879. That's a letter addressed to the Crisis Staff of the region from the president of the Crisis Staff of Petrovac signed by Mr. Novakovic. You knew Mr. Novakovic presumably?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you've told us that you would have dealt with correspondence that came to the crisis staff. What is the letter headed? Would you like to read it out, please, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Implementation of steps and decisions set in the Crisis Staff session of 22nd of June 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the next line, please. Read the next line aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to item II of the Krajina AR Crisis Staff decision dated the 22nd of June 1992, we hereby inform you that the following steps from item I of the decision has been implemented in the territory of our municipality."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that does go on to explain how they've dismissed the people in accordance with that decision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So are you telling us, Mr. Blagojevic, as you did a little time ago, that no municipality reported on what steps they had taken?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really didn't remember. I couldn't remember, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need to clear this up, because yesterday, if you remember, Ms. Korner, I did put to the witness two questions. One relating to the Municipal Assemblies, and the other relating to the municipal crisis staffs. And if I remember well, what he conceded was that practically in all the municipalities, the municipal assemblies had gone into hibernation. They had been replaced by the municipal crisis staffs. And then when he had stated earlier on that no implementation of the regional crisis staff had taken place, he meant the municipal assemblies and not the municipal crisis staffs. And he did concede yesterday that implementation did take place by the municipal crisis staffs. That's what I understood yesterday. The decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff were not implemented by the municipal assemblies, but were implemented by the municipal crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour may be right. We had better understand from Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you agree with what I have just stated, basing myself on what you had --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely, Mr. President. That's what I was thinking. That the municipal assemblies at their meetings didn't put that forward, and the crisis staff of the municipalities, except for this -- actually, I don't know whether any other reports came in with respect to this. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, we can deal with quite a large topic that I have lined up for you in one simple question. Is it your evidence that to your knowledge, the municipal crisis staffs implemented the decisions made by the regional crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't remember whether they fully implemented those decisions. I just don't remember. I haven't any knowledge or awareness of it. I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who implemented the decisions of the regional crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. President, I didn't get any feed -- there was no feedback information. Except for what it says here, I really can't remember whether there was any feedback information coming in to the effect that they were informing the crisis staff and that we did such and such in conformity with your decision. I really can't remember whether there was -- whether the municipalities did give out information about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, the reason that the meetings were being held which were attended by the presidents of the municipalities is so that they could inform the crisis staff of what was happening in their region and what they were doing about the directions given by the crisis staff. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually at those meetings, they would indicate the state of affairs in their municipality and any problems they were encountering. And there were also cases where it said "pursuant to the crisis staff decision, let us see how the municipality was being supplied with food, oil derivatives, medicines and so on." The army with cigarettes, that kind of thing. And then I told you how the discussions would evolve. They would say "we don't have this or we're lacking in that or we don't have the facilities for the other."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but in these lengthy discussions, these meetings that went on for days and days and days, was one of the subjects touched upon what the municipal crisis staffs were doing to carry out the instructions of the regional crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. When, for example, they discussed the problem of --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Blagojevic. Let's not have probably. You are able to remember things like what Kupresanin said. You were present at those meetings. Is that what was happening, amongst other things, that reports were being given?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That reports -- that the municipalities tabled reports? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That the municipalities reported to the regional crisis staff, to Mr. Brdjanin, about what was being done in their area to carry out the instructions like this one?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at these meetings, there was most probably talk of that, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to pursue this any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I feel like being in a dental clinic rather than in a courtroom, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Can we move on, because I need to finish today, Mr. Blagojevic, with you. The funds, let's deal with that now, you asserted -- the only thing you're very sure of is that nobody took any notice of the order that funds should be given to the autonomous region. Is that still your evidence?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the executive council was set up, it informed all the secretariats, and laws were applied at that time passed by the National Assembly, that is to say laws on taxation, various transactions, commerce and so on. So the resources that were supposed to be paid into the republican budget would remain in the area of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and placed in the service of.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you were taken through a number of decisions by Mr. Cunningham that were orders to the municipalities to supply funds to the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff or whatever. And you said, you were positive about that, and I can read back your words, no funds were paid. Is that still your evidence?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so. That is the decision by which the municipalities were supposed to have 30 dinars per inhabitant paid in. There were no technical reasons or any rules and regulations according to which they could put that into practice because they paid in regular taxes and contributions on the basis of the law governing income taxes and turnover taxes, taxes on goods and services. And so those taxes, those funds, went to the social accounting service in Banja Luka, and those funds were supposed to go to the budget of the Federation. However, the executive council didn't send those funds to the Republic budget, but kept them back in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Could you have a look, please, at Exhibit P2107. Just have a look at it, and then I'll ask you the question. Perhaps it better be moved up the ELMO so that... Yes, can we go to the next. All right, Mr. Blagojevic. Does that show that the Municipality of Bosanska Krupa on the 10th of July complied with the decision of the crisis staff on the 13th of May to pay 3 dinars per citizen a month?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the conclusions of the crisis staff, it was stated that 30 dinars per month per citizen should be paid in. 30 dinars per capita. Whereas here I see it says 3 dinars. So 10 times less than the 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You said no funds -- whether it may be a typing error or not is neither here nor there. You said no funds were ever paid in as a result of this decision. But do you agree that you were wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really didn't remember this. I didn't even know about this. Because here, I can see 3, whereas 30 was what was prescribed. And I believe that this municipality did not even have any money. I don't know whether they had any money at their disposal at all, any funds. Because there were just a few municipalities that funded the entire region, Banja Luka, Gradiska, Laktasi, Srbac, Prnjavor, Mrkonjic Grad, Bosanska Dubica. These were the only places where something was going on. Prijedor. Novi. This particular municipality, the Serbian Municipality of Krupa, I don't know where they are today. The entire territory of that municipality is just one village. There are no economic entities there. The total number of voters there is not more than a hundred. So I suppose --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Blagojevic. That will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's take advantage of the fact that his memory seems to be coming back, Ms. Korner. We'll have a 25-minute break. In the meantime, if you have any other documents in line on this matter, you can prepare them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, but I think he was going to be given -- he wants to identify his signature in the same bunch of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Usher, could you escort the witness out of the courtroom, please. Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I will have redirect. I just wanted to let the Court know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine so. Thank you. 25 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On LiveNote, page 68, line 22, that's when the Court starts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. 68. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's when Your Honour made some statements with respect to your recollection of testimony from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And while I typically rely on the Court's recollection, I think -- I just wanted -- my perception, my recollection of the testimony yesterday is different from that that you expressed, and I just wanted to note that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And it's okay with the Court, Witness Number 17 will follow the witness next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, can we come back to witnesses at the end of the session. I mean, I'm delighted to hear that Witness Number 17, if it's the man I think it is, is coming, but I'd like to know about the following week, but I'll leave it till the end of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yesterday, just to clear this up, Mr. Cunningham, I had asked the witness "Were the Municipal Assemblies meeting at the time or were they in hibernation because of the existence of crisis staffs in all the municipalities?" The witness said: "Probably they had to freeze their activities, so there were no sessions due to the government's decision on the establishment of crisis staffs." And then I said: "So wouldn't it have been logical and reasonable in a time of great crisis that the crisis staffs of the Autonomous Region of Krajina to make sure that the decisions and conclusions are adopted, are implemented, that the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina be amended?" Since the Municipal Assemblies were not meeting, and therefore, could not adopt or approve the decisions taken by the ARK Crisis Staff, was that the situation to be accepted, to be kept, to be tolerated in a time of crisis, or a situation which needed a remedy, the remedy being the amendment to the statute that was adopted on decision number 42. The witness said: "Since the assemblies could not hold the meetings then the crisis staff of each municipality was supposed to ratify this." And then I said: "So I would take it if I were to show you documents of conclusions or decisions taken by the municipal crisis staffs adopting, endorsing the decisions taken by the ARK Crisis Staff, would that mean that the municipal crisis staff were implementing the decisions of the ARK crisis staff or not to you?" And the witness said: "If they ratified them at the sessions, I suppose they were in a position to implement them." This is what was said yesterday. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, can I come back to witnesses at the end of the session? I regret that -- I didn't think the witness is going to finish today, unless Your Honours will order me. But I've got a number of more topics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I were you, Ms. Korner, I would bring it to a quick end, as quickly as possible, my suggestion is. And I think the situation being what it is, I would rather prefer to have -- to hear what the re-examination is about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, Your Honour, there are a number of topics that I really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. I'm not going to foreclose on you, but I have told you what my preference is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we deal with the meetings themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: A few topics, please, Mr. Blagojevic. General Talic didn't attend very often, but sent Colonel Vojinovic to represent him at the meetings. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you told us in interview at page 35, Mr. Cunningham, that at the one meeting you remember Talic attending, apart from the problem of conscripts and the problems between the military authorities and the deputies, it was put to you that at the same meeting, Talic made many requests to the crisis staff regarding food and housing for the soldiers. And your reply was: "Yes, he said that he was having huge problems." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As far as the paramilitaries were concerned, and this was a topic that went on for some time in the meetings, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It wasn't, was it, the Serbian paramilitaries, Arkan's forces, the White Eagles, the Wolves of Prnjavor that were being discussed, but what were called the Muslim paramilitaries, the Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this be in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into -- let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The camps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The camps, Mr. Blagojevic, you've told us there was never any discussion about the camps at any of the meetings you attended. Do you still want to adhere to that answer?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember that these matters were ever discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, as the president of the crisis staff, made a visit, didn't he, to, among other places, Omarska?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Did you not read not anything in the newspapers or on television about Mr. Brdjanin and other politicians visiting Omarska?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You do, however, remember Mr. Kupresanin, your direct boss of the assembly, visiting camps, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin went to Omarska. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Took out of Omarska a deputy -- a Bosniak deputy called Mevludin Sejmenovic. Is that right? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he went to Manjaca as well, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't. I am aware of the visit to Omarska because I witnessed him bringing Mr. Sejmenovic back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you go to Omarska as well?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How did you witness him bringing Mr. Sejmenovic back, then?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He brought Mr. Sejmenovic to his office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So Mr. Kupresanin, Mr. Radic, and Mr. Brdjanin, who had all been to these camps, according to you - is that what you're saying - never raised in any meeting the fact that Prijedor was running a camp that clearly, as you now know, if not before, was a disgrace?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, if I might just -- I have an objection because the question states that Mr. Brdjanin has been to all of these camps, and that's not true. I understand what she is trying to do, but I just wanted to register an objection to that part of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I have to sustain the objection, Ms. Korner. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, who had been to Omarska, never raised in a meeting the fact that this was a disgraceful camp?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin, who I suggest to you went to Omarska and to Manjaca, never raised the fact that two camps were being run where prisoners were in a disgraceful condition?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did, when he brought Mr. Sejmenovic back. He talked about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In a meeting of the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. N

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So when did he talk about that?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he brought Mr. Sejmenovic back to his office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So he, then, told you what the conditions in Omarska were like?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ask him whether he was going to raise that in a crisis staff meeting at which the leaders of the Prijedor Municipality would be attending?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't. This was simply not within my purview. I was not a political figure to raise any such issue or suggest anything to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because the authorities, representatives of the authorities in Prijedor, did attend the crisis staff meetings, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was there anything to prevent Mr. Kupresanin or Mr. Brdjanin saying to these people "these camps are a disgrace; you must close them down or clean them up"?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There was a certain competition between the people from Prijedor and those from the Banja Luka region. There was a sort of animosity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand that's what you're saying anyhow. What was to prevent them, Mr. Kupresanin, from saying to Mr. Stakic or Simo Drljaca or Srdjo Srdic or any of those -- Kovacevic, that camp is a positive disgrace?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I want you to look, please, briefly at Document Number P229. This was sent -- this document was sent to the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Banja Luka. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it was clear, wasn't it, that the municipalities were urging the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff to become even more extreme in its attitudes?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this document was discussed, wasn't it, at a meeting of the crisis staff on either the following day or the day after. That's the 8th, 9th of June. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether this was...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Mr. Blagojevic, isn't it one of the reasons why Colonel Vojinovic was told that the Muslims in the military in the VRS had to be dismissed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you not remember Colonel Vojinovic attending a meeting of the crisis staff not long after this where it was made plain that the crisis staffs wanted non-Serbs in the military to be dismissed?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not aware of that. I know that there were a lot of Bosniak and Croat officers in the army, and this is what was said to Mr. Vojinovic. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you know the names of Colonel Selak and Colonel Hasotic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, at the end of this period, on the 17th of July, all the decisions taken by the crisis staff were put to the assembly for verification, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, have a look, please, at Exhibit 285.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. It's one of the documents you provided to the Office of the Prosecutor, isn't it? And we can see that, if you put it that way, the great and the good attended this meeting: Talic, Hadzic from the Croatian Krajina, Martic from the Croatian Krajina, Subotic, Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Kalinic, and General Ninkovic. And if we look, please, at item number 4, verification of the decisions and conclusions adopted by the Crisis Staff and war presidency of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, there was a debate and -- sorry. Following a debate in which several assembly members took part all decisions and conclusions adopted by the crisis staff and the war presidency of the Autonomous Region of Krajina were verified. There was one brave man who stood out against them. So that gave, Mr. Blagojevic, according to you, did it not, full authority and legality to the decisions taken by the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Including the decision signed by Mr. Brdjanin personally which you didn't put into the Gazette?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The one of the 22nd June.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And including the alteration to the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina which said that the municipalities that you were shown yesterday, the municipalities had to obey - and I'm paraphrasing now - the instructions of the region. That's right, isn't it, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Will you finish in 20 minutes, Mr. Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'll try, because I know the witness wants to get home. So I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The first area I want to go over with you is in response to the Prosecutor's question with respect to correspondence that the ARK Crisis Staff may or may not have ever received. Did you ever receive any correspondence -- when I say you, I'm referring to the ARK Crisis Staff, receive any correspondence from the RS saying -- ordering them to disband the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You remember giving your statement to the OTP in Banja Luka in July of 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant was that they never delivered it, if you know what I mean. They never sent any letters to the Crisis Staff, that is, representatives of the government or the presidency. That's the way I understood your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. So no correspondence from the republic -- from the RS. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Korner showed you a document that I believe is Prosecutor Exhibit 2107. That is the exhibit, I believe, from the Petrovac Crisis Staff dated 10 July 1992 dealing with their allocation of 3 dinars per person for funds. Do you remember that exhibit? And the usher's going to -- it's actually --

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it only a little while ago. However, given their economic strength, I doubt whether they ever paid a single dinar into any funds.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I want to remind you, I'm assuming that you would like to be at home with your family for the weekend. So if you listen to my questions, there's a good chance you could be out of here to be with your family. So just listen. So your testimony today is this letter -- this document which came from Krupa, I stand corrected on that, this is the first time you had ever seen the document? Or you just didn't remember seeing it before.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long time ago, as you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Listen to the question. Was there any other correspondence on this topic, that is, satisfying the conclusion of the ARK on 13 May 1992, was there any other correspondence, any or report from any other municipality? Do you ever remember getting anything else?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Page 9 of the LiveNote today, Ms. Korner was asking you about the attendance of certain members of the Crisis Staff covering a topic that I had covered with you yesterday. And in your testimony yesterday, you couldn't recall how many times such people as Stojan Zupljanin, Mr. Mirjanic, Mr. Puvacic, Mr. Dubocanin, Stevandic, and Djuro Bulic attended. When I asked you about your statement in Banja Luka that we have been referring to, did you ever get a complete copy of this statement?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Never had a chance to read the entire thing to refresh your recollection, did you?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the one of the 19th?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Right. The one that we've seen bits and pieces of on the screen in front of you. You didn't have a chance to look at it and refresh your recollection. And the reason that I'm asking that, in your testimony - excuse me, in your statement to the OTP from July of 2001 - you could recall there how many times certain people attended the meetings. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it yesterday. These people attended, as far as I can remember, only a couple of times. Later on, it turned out -- into meetings attended by the deputies, the presidents of the municipalities --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I really want to get you home. I know you miss your family, so bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'd like to show him his statement in B/C/S to refresh his recollection because I want to ask him questions about -- because he answers in the statement specifically how much certain witnesses attended. Excuse me, certain members attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm on page 16 of the English version. And on the middle of page 16, on line 14 - and I'm sorry, Mr. Usher, I can't give you the exact page of the Serbian version, but I think it is going to be about one page ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would it be quicker if he just puts to him how many times he says each person attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: In your statement, sir, and I want to see if this refreshes your recollection, you were asked specifically how often did Stojan Zupljanin attend. And I want to see if this refreshes your recollection. You said that I think that Stojan Zupljanin attended one session, one meeting. I can't recall properly, but I think it was one. Does that refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And I adhere to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to Dr. Mirjanic, you said that he attended around ten times. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which doctor?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Dr. Mirjanic.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. Because I can remember things much better then than I can now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And understandable. With respect to Milan Puvacic, you said that he "attended only a few times." Does that refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And with respect to Jovo Rosic, you said at line 21 "the same thing, maybe a few times". Does that refresh your recollection there?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And with respect to Dubocanin, you said that "maybe he attended six or seven, eight meetings." Does that sound -- refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And you gave the same answer when the name of Mr. Stevandic was brought up, the same several times was your answer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. It was a long time ago. 12 and a half years. And it's very hard for me to be precise on some facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fair. On page 15 and 16 of the LiveNote today, Ms. Korner discussed with you in the case of Milorad Sajic, the regional secretariat for National Defence, do you recall if that body, those regional secretariat for defence, whether they were abolished in May?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. But I seem to feel that the amendments to the law on national defence, that Articles 37 to 53 were deleted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. You were asked several times about reports from municipalities. And towards the end of Ms. Korner's cross-examination, she specifically asked you about the attendance of representatives from Prijedor. Do you recall how often -- or how would you characterise the attendance by the Prijedor representatives? Were they there at every meeting? What do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite certainly, they didn't attend every meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. And do you remember in your statement to the OTP at page 20 being asked what would happen if Mr. Rasula or Srdjo Srdic showed up at crisis staff meetings? Do you remember what you told the OTP? Because if you don't, I'll put the question to you directly to see if it refreshes your recollection.

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Srdjo was there several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you remember making this statement to the OTP, page 20, when asked about Mr. Rasula and Srdjo Srdic attending crisis staff meetings? And I'm going to pick it up at line 20, and I'm quoting you. "Because" -- well, I'll read the entire answer. "Well, if they were in Banja Luka and there was a meeting or a session of the crisis staff in Banja Luka at that time, then they would drop by. Because deputies would usually come to have a cup of coffee with Mr. Kupresanin, and then when they visited him and if the crisis staff organised a meeting, then Mr. Kupresanin would say to them, `well, we have a meeting with the crisis staff, and there is a session today, and you could attend it and you can also express your own problems'. They would come to see Vojo and criticise government. They would tell him about troubles how the government forgot about them, how the government isn't helping them, and basically how they criticised the government." Does that refresh your recollection of what you told the OTP in Banja Luka in July of 2001?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. What you just read out. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Do you ever remember at any of these meetings Mr. Srdjo, any representative from Prijedor or any municipality that had the camps, ever bringing anything up about the camps?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When you found out about Omarska, because Mr. Kupresanin had brought the gentleman back from Omarska, do you happen to recall whether or not the crisis staff even was in existence when you found out about Omarska?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Fair enough. Ms. Korner asked you questions with respect to the crisis staff decisions and the signatures thereon. Were other members -- was it agreed by members of the crisis staff that someone other than Mr. Brdjanin could sign crisis staff decision?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a decision was made authorising the secretary to prepare the Official Gazette. And in the absence of someone, one of the members, that someone else could sign. I happened to remember that actually yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I want to go back now to Prosecutor's Exhibit 2107 and just have that available to you because that is the decision from the Bosanska Krupa Crisis Staff in response to the request for payment of a per capita payment of dinars. First of all, do you know whether or not the crisis staff ever opened any sort of banking account, had made any sort of banking arrangements for the receipt of any money related to this per capita request?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There was just the giro account of the assembly itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Was there -- although this crisis staff decision says that Krupa has allocated 3 dinars per person, do you know whether that money was ever forwarded to the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember whether any of this was ever implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. You also told us that the amount offered was 10 times less than that requested. Do you know whether the crisis staff ever sanctioned the Municipality of Krupa or its crisis staff for their response?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've just remembered that probably that money was never paid in because on the account of the assembly, there were no funds, and we sought funds from the federal executive council of the region, or rather, the government of the autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: There is some confusion in my mind, so help me out here. Did any other municipality even respond to this request for a per capita, 30 dinar payment?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I've just remembered. After the 4th of March 1992, all the funds could be paid in only on the giro accounts of the executive council of the region, because in actual fact that was the government of the autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Two or three more brief topics. Ms. Korner talked to you about Serbian paramilitaries and other paramilitaries in the context of crisis staff orders. I would like the usher to show you P227, which is the ARK Gazette. Go to entry number 15 - excuse me - it's entry for 15 May 1992, and I'll find the page. The English translation, the page is 20. Conclusion number 3, I'll read it to you very slowly, it says: "Especially strict measures shall be implemented against any person misusing uniform and insignia of police, TO, or army, and without authorisation stopping, checking people's identities or vehicles, searching dwellings or other premises." By the way that that conclusion is phrased, would that be directed to Serbian paramilitaries or to non-Serbian paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the conclusion which refers to the Serbian paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: The final area that I want to talk to you has to deal with -- Prosecutor showed you Exhibit P229. And to refresh your recollection, Prosecutor's P229 is a conclusion dated 17 June 1992 from the Sanska -- 7 June, I apologise, from what has been known as the Sanska Una subregion. And this was showed to you. And it was put to you in something along these lines. Isn't this a request for the crisis staff to become even more extreme? Do you remember that being asked of you just -- no more than 20 minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Do you happen to know what -- whether there was a subsequent document, specifically Prosecutor's 247, that was also issued by the same region? If we can have you look at that very briefly, then, Judge, that will be my very, very last area. If we can just finish this, then I'll be done. Have you ever seen this document? Were you aware of it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORO BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's all I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've actually got the original of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's another photocopy, but still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I would suggest it's shown to the witness, and that will be your final statement for today. Give it to him straight away. You are being shown, Mr. Blagojevic, the best that the Prosecution can show you. Do you recognise your signature on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's possible. I'm not sure. I'm really not sure, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, all right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it's not the original. This is a copy, after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Okay. So you can take the document back, please. Mr. Blagojevic, both Judge Janu, Judge Taya, and myself had several questions to put to you. But we've heard from Mr. Cunningham that you would like to be back with your family as soon as possible. And we will accommodate you. We will not be asking you any questions. You're free to go. But before the usher accompanies you out of this courtroom, on behalf of the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for having come over to give your testimony. You will be escorted by the usher, and you will receive all the attention and assistance you require in order to enable you to return back to Banja Luka at the earliest possible opportunity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I be allowed to thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that I thank this distinguished Tribunal for giving me the honour of testifying here for three days, and to try, because after all, it has been 12 and a half years since the events, to testify to the best of my recollections, and to have us clarify certain facts for the Tribunal really to gain an insight into the legal and relevant state of affairs. And I really do extend my gratitude to the distinguished President and his colleagues, to the Prosecution, and also to the Defence counsel and all the other people who have helped me here in these past few days at the Tribunal because I do feel proud of having come here and being given the opportunity of saying something after 12 and a half years and presenting some facts here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We also wish you a safe journey back home. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know it's running over slightly, but I'll ask for Your Honours' and the interpreters' indulgence over this question of witnesses, as I understand it, the witness who is scheduled to come next week and will be followed by Witness Number 17. I wanted to know who is coming after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I was about to tell you. 29. 32.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, finally, then, Glamoc, Srbac, Laktasi, are we going to hear from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I talked to Mr. Ackerman about that, the final agreement had not been reached. I think our agreement was that we will let them know by Monday, and we will let you know by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, Mr. Cunningham, Ms. Korner, for all the cooperation that you have shown in order to enable this witness to return home before the weekend. It is my duty, however, to thank the interpreters, the rest of technical staff, all the rest of the staff, particularly, I repeat, the usher, without all your cooperation we wouldn't have finished. So I thank you all. We meet Monday in the afternoon. Thank you. I don't know which courtroom. I still have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of November, 2003, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.52 p.m.
